% --- latex-dual-layer macros (auto-generated) ---
\newlength{\dlboxwidth}
\newlength{\dlboxheight}
\newlength{\dlboxdepth}
\newcommand{\duallayerbox}[2]{%
  \begingroup
  \settowidth{\dlboxwidth}{\strut #1}%
  \settoheight{\dlboxheight}{\strut #1}%
  \settodepth{\dlboxdepth}{\strut #1}%
  \ifdim\dlboxwidth=0pt
    \settowidth{\dlboxwidth}{#2}%
  \fi
  \raisebox{0pt}[\dlboxheight][\dlboxdepth]{%
    \makebox[\dlboxwidth][l]{\resizebox{\dlboxwidth}{!}{\strut #2}}%
  }%
  \endgroup
}

\section*{Multiple Choice (36 marks)}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\item Seven people \duallayerbox{standing silently}{chatting loudly} while waiting for a bus at a bus stop is an example of which of the following?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item \duallayerbox{A primary group}{A secondary group}
    \item \duallayerbox{A secondary group}{A primary group}
    \item \duallayerbox{An aggregate}{A primary group}
    \item \duallayerbox{A social category}{An aggregate}
\end{enumerate}
\item Chodorow (1978) argued that \duallayerbox{gender socialization}{cultural assimilation} occurred through:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item both boys and girls being \duallayerbox{closely attached to their mothers}{distant from their mothers}, but then boys breaking away
    \item \duallayerbox{girls being attached to their mothers}{boys being attached to their fathers} but then breaking away
    \item \duallayerbox{boys being attached to their fathers}{girls being attached to their fathers} and girls to their mothers
    \item both boys and girls being \duallayerbox{closely attached to their fathers}{distant from their fathers}, but girls breaking away
\end{enumerate}
\item The media-themes model of \duallayerbox{media influence}{cultural influence} claims that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item audiences \duallayerbox{selectively interpret}{passively absorb} what they want to hear
    \item \duallayerbox{content analysis}{survey methods} is the best way to identify the themes covered by the media
    \item audiences \duallayerbox{passively absorb}{actively critique} whatever messages they are given
    \item social interaction \duallayerbox{reinforces}{challenges} the ideas and images that audiences select
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{A moral panic}{A social movement} occurs when:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item the media \duallayerbox{exaggerate}{downplay} reports of deviant groups, generating hostile reactions
    \item children \duallayerbox{watch violent or sexually explicit films}{read educational books} and then copy the behaviour
    \item audiences \duallayerbox{challenge}{reinforce} the ethnic stereotypes represented by the media
    \item elitists express concern with the \duallayerbox{Americanization}{globalization} of culture
\end{enumerate}
\item Someone who gains a higher (or lower) social position than he or she was born into has experienced
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item absolute poverty
    \item relative poverty
    \item vertical mobility
    \item horizontal mobility
\end{enumerate}
\item The capitalist world economy is what Wallerstein (1974) would call a 'world system'. This term refers to:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item a means of transporting money between different areas of a country
    \item an empire with a bureaucratic administration but no political centre
    \item an awareness of risks and dangers that affect the environment as a whole
    \item a unit with a division of labour that extends across ethnic and cultural groups
\end{enumerate}
\item In Symbolic Interactionist theory, Mead defined the 'generalized other' as:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item the group of structural theories of society that he was reacting against
    \item the overall impression of ourselves that we try to give off to others
    \item a significant figure in early childhood who teaches us the general values of society
    \item an image of how people in the wider society might perceive our behaviour
\end{enumerate}
\item In the traditional hierarchy of status and precedence, which of these members of the upper class are in the right order (from highest to lowest status)?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item Prime Minister, Archbishop of York, Viscounts of England
    \item Marquesses of England, Earls of Great Britain, King's Brothers
    \item Esquires, Serjeants of Law, Dukes' Eldest Sons
    \item King's Grandsons, Lord High Treasurer, Companions of the Bath
\end{enumerate}
\item Marx (1844) claimed that capitalism had alienated workers from:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item the product they were making
    \item the production process
    \item each other and humanity in general
    \item all of the above
\end{enumerate}
\item According to Davis (1995), women may seek cosmetic surgery because:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item they have a deep-rooted sense of ineffectiveness and are striving for control
    \item they are in pursuit of the 'perfect' body, fuelled by images of beauty
    \item they perceive a part of their body as stigmatizing, in relation to a cultural ideal
    \item their male partners pressurize them to look like supermodels
\end{enumerate}
\item Which of the following was not part of Weber's ideal type of bureaucracy?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item impersonal rules
    \item extensive paperwork
    \item hierarchy of officials
    \item Salaries
\end{enumerate}
\item Economic aid has largely failed to promote modernization in the developing countries because:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item there are no clearly defined projects into which the money can be directed
    \item the United Nations has refused to call on rich countries to provide it
    \item debt repayments with interest can be greater than the amount of money received
    \item debt repayments with interest can be greater than the amount of money received
\end{enumerate}
\item Marriage appears to be in decline because:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item the proportion of people living alone has fallen to 29\%
    \item many people are cohabiting in long term relationships
    \item the upward curve of remarriages compensates for the drop in first marriages
    \item all of the above
\end{enumerate}
\item Weber (1919) said that the state's monopoly of the use of force was legitimated by:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item charismatic authority
    \item rational-legal authority
    \item traditional authority
    \item value-rational authority
\end{enumerate}
\item World-affirming religions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item embrace conventional cultural values but offer new means of achieving them
    \item react against the loss of any meaningful religious content in the teachings of churches
    \item adopt an attitude of mild disapproval towards mainstream social values
    \item reject both the goals and means of conventional society and provide utopian alternatives
\end{enumerate}
\item Disciplinary power was exercised in the 19th century factories by:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item the use of corporal punishment by employers
    \item excluding women from participating in waged labour
    \item punctuality, uninterrupted work and the threat of dismissal
    \item making routine tasks less monotonous
\end{enumerate}
\item Herberg's (1955) study of religion in America suggested that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item ethnic minorities practised religion to achieve social acceptance in the culture
    \item mainstream faiths were becoming increasingly identified with national identity
    \item the moral teachings of the main religions were becoming relatively similar
    \item all of the above
\end{enumerate}
\item Becker proclaimed that cannabis use was:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item increasing throughout all sections of youth in the 1970s
    \item learned gradually through the social processes of a deviant career
    \item a dangerous pastime that young people should not be allowed to pursue
    \item not as enjoyable as other sociologists had suggested
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

\section*{True / False (4 marks)}
\textit{Answer True or False and justify briefly.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\item True or False: The correct answer to 'Scientific management involved:' is 'the subdivision of labour into small tasks'.
\item True or False: The correct answer to 'The 1944 Education Act provided:' is 'free secondary education for all'.
\end{enumerate}
